podcast.title: Considered "Too Light" for Punk
podcast.body: In the mid-2000s bifurcation of pop punk, Good Charlotte was identified as being "too light" or "too poppy for punk." This led to some alt-rock radio stations refusing to play their music, claiming they appealed to the "wrong kind of people" (i.e., fans who were too young). "groups like Headley and Simple Plan and Good Charlotte were maybe a little too light."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influenced by Blink-182
podcast.body: Good Charlotte is listed among the artists who have been notably influenced by Blink-182, highlighting the impact of Blink-182's sound and career on the development of other bands in the pop punk scene. "Some 41 good Charlotte simple-plan panic at the disco, followed boy, headly, billy talent, you would meet six, paramour, you know, you get the idea."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Initial Acceptance and Later Rejection
podcast.body: Good Charlotte initially received positive reception within the pop punk scene. However, they were eventually "damned by the audience," who began to dismiss their music with terms like "kitty punk." "Good Charlotte started out as being fine, but were eventually show to damn by the audience."

xref.title: Influence on Pop Punk
xref.body: Blink-182 is considered one of the most influential pop punk bands of the 21st century. Their style and career trajectory have left a significant mark on numerous artists across the genre, inspiring bands like Sum 41, Good Charlotte, Simple Plan, Panic! At The Disco, Fall Out Boy, Hedley, Billy Talent, You Me At Six, and Paramore. "Blink has to be considered one of the most influential pop punk bands of the 21st century."
